set1.io: Describe adverse effects of antiarrhythmic drugs
set1.q: A 62-year-old woman on amiodarone for a year reports fatigue, weight gain and feeling cold all the time. Which listed toxicity best fits?
opts: Correct. Amiodarone is an analog of thyroid hormone, and its thyroid abnormalities run in both directions; fatigue, weight gain and cold intolerance fit hypothyroidism.
Amiodarone can cause hyperthyroidism too, but that brings weight loss and heat intolerance; her picture is hypothyroidism.
Hepatic dysfunction is on amiodarone's list but does not explain cold intolerance and weight gain; this is hypothyroidism.
Neuropathy is an amiodarone neurotoxicity, with weakness and ataxia, not cold intolerance; this is hypothyroidism.

set1.io: Identify indications for commonly used antiarrhythmic drugs
set1.q: A 28-year-old woman has sudden palpitations; her electrocardiogram shows a regular narrow-complex tachycardia, diagnosed as paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia. Vagal maneuvers fail. Which drug is listed to terminate it?
opts: Lidocaine is not effective against atrial arrhythmias and is used for ventricular ones; adenosine is listed for this tachycardia.
ruled out by a stated finding
Correct. Adenosine is listed for paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia; it hyperpolarizes cells and may stop the heart for 2 to 3 seconds.
Magnesium sulfate is listed for torsades de pointes; paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia is an adenosine indication.
Dofetilide is listed for normal rhythm in atrial fibrillation and needs special training; adenosine terminates this tachycardia.

set1.io: Describe absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of antiarrhythmic drugs
set1.q: A 74-year-old man with severely reduced kidney function has atrial fibrillation. Which rhythm drug is most affected by his kidneys, being mainly eliminated unchanged there?
opts: Correct. Dofetilide is mainly eliminated unchanged in the kidneys.
Verapamil undergoes hepatic metabolism, so its caution is liver damage; dofetilide is eliminated unchanged by the kidneys.
Lidocaine has extensive first-pass metabolism, which is why it is given intravenously; dofetilide leaves by the kidneys.
Amiodarone's listed kinetics are slow onset and slow elimination over a 40-day half-life; dofetilide is the one eliminated unchanged by the kidneys.

set1.io: Outline appropriate patient education for antiarrhythmic drugs
set1.q: A 34-year-old man is about to receive adenosine for paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia. Which effects should he be told to expect?
opts: Tinnitus and dizziness with blurred vision are quinidine's cinchonism; adenosine brings flushing and chest burning.
Correct. Adenosine's listed toxicities are flushing (20%), shortness of breath and burning in the chest; the heart may also pause briefly.
Drowsiness, confusion and muscle twitches are lidocaine toxicity; adenosine brings flushing and chest burning.
Sedation and fatigue are listed for metoprolol and acebutolol; adenosine brings flushing and chest burning.

set1.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of antiarrhythmic drugs
set1.q: A 55-year-old man taking propafenone develops a sore throat and fever, and his blood count shows almost no neutrophils. Which listed adverse effect is this?
opts: Thrombocytopenia is on propafenone's list too, but it lowers platelets; absent neutrophils are agranulocytosis.
A lupus-like syndrome is procainamide's, in slow acetylators; absent neutrophils on propafenone are agranulocytosis.
Correct. Propafenone's toxicity list includes agranulocytosis, anemia and thrombocytopenia.
Bronchospasm comes from propafenone's beta-blocking activity and does not lower neutrophils; this is agranulocytosis.

set1.q: A 64-year-old man had a myocardial infarction two years ago and now has frequent premature ventricular contractions. Which drug should be avoided because it raises mortality after a myocardial infarction?
opts: Propranolol lists myocardial infarction among its indications, not as a reason to avoid it; flecainide raises mortality after one.
Metoprolol is a beta-1 selective blocker similar to propranolol, with no mortality warning after infarction; flecainide carries it.
ruled out by a stated finding
Amiodarone is listed for recurrent ventricular arrhythmias resistant to other drugs; the increased mortality after infarction is flecainide's.
Correct. Flecainide's toxicity list includes increased mortality after a myocardial infarction, and it is used only without significant structural heart damage.

set1.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of antiarrhythmic drugs
set1.q: A 78-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation takes digoxin, and amiodarone was added two weeks ago. She now has anorexia, nausea, confusion and visual disturbances. Which is the most likely cause?
opts: Amiodarone neurotoxicity is neuropathy, muscle weakness and ataxia, not anorexia and confusion; amiodarone raised her digoxin level instead.
Correct. Amiodarone increases digoxin, and digoxin toxicity lists nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and anorexia with confusion, delirium, headache, seizures and visual disturbances.
Amiodarone's thyroid abnormalities do not explain visual disturbances with nausea; it raises digoxin, so this is digoxin toxicity.
Cinchonism (tinnitus, dizziness, blurred vision) comes from quinidine, which she does not take; this is digoxin toxicity.
ruled out by a stated finding

set1.io: Describe absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of antiarrhythmic drugs
set1.q: A 63-year-old man with cirrhosis has paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia, and verapamil is considered. Why is caution needed?
opts: Correct. Verapamil and diltiazem undergo hepatic metabolism, so caution is advised in liver damage.
It is cleared unchanged by the kidneys
Elimination unchanged by the kidneys is dofetilide's route; verapamil needs caution in liver damage because the liver metabolizes it.
Pulmonary fibrosis is amiodarone's toxicity; verapamil needs caution in cirrhosis because of hepatic metabolism.
It is acetylated to an active metabolite
Acetylation to an active metabolite describes procainamide; verapamil needs caution in cirrhosis because of hepatic metabolism.

set1.io: Describe adverse effects of antiarrhythmic drugs
set1.q: A 57-year-old woman with asthma is started on propranolol for a supraventricular arrhythmia. Two days later she is wheezing. Which property of propranolol explains this?
opts: Beta-1 selectivity, as with metoprolol, causes less bronchospasm; propranolol is nonselective.
Correct. Propranolol is a nonselective beta blocker, and bronchospasm is on its toxicity list.
Potassium channel block with beta blockade is sotalol's combination; propranolol's bronchospasm comes from being nonselective.
Propranolol is described as membrane stabilizing, but its bronchospasm comes from nonselective beta blockade.

set1.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for antiarrhythmic drugs
set1.q: A 69-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation is started on dofetilide to restore normal rhythm. Which finding needs the closest watch?
opts: Corneal deposits are an amiodarone toxicity; the finding to watch on dofetilide is QT prolongation.
Thrombocytopenia is listed for quinidine, flecainide and propafenone; the finding to watch on dofetilide is QT prolongation.
Blue-gray skin is an amiodarone toxicity; the finding to watch on dofetilide is QT prolongation.
Correct. Dofetilide's listed adverse effects are marked QT prolongation and torsades de pointes (1 to 3%).

set1.io: Identify indications for commonly used antiarrhythmic drugs
set1.q: A 62-year-old man in the coronary unit with an acute myocardial infarction has frequent ventricular premature beats arising from ischemic tissue. Which class I drug works best on sodium channels in ischemic tissue?
opts: Flecainide affects the normal heart and raises mortality after a myocardial infarction; lidocaine works best in ischemic tissue.
ruled out by a stated finding
Quinidine is a class IA drug with no ischemic-tissue selectivity and many toxicities; lidocaine works best in ischemic tissue.
Correct. Lidocaine (class IB) is given intravenously and is most effective on sodium channels in ischemic tissue, with less effect on normal tissue.
Disopyramide is a class IA drug with negative inotropic effects that can worsen heart failure; lidocaine targets ischemic tissue.

set1.io: Describe absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of antiarrhythmic drugs
set1.q: A 72-year-old man in the intensive care unit after surgery has a supraventricular tachycardia. The team wants an intravenous beta blocker whose effect wears off quickly. Which drug fits?
opts: Propranolol is the nonselective beta blocker used as the class II example; the intravenous short-acting one is esmolol.
Metoprolol is a beta-1 selective blocker with less bronchospasm; the intravenous short-acting beta blocker is esmolol.
Sotalol adds potassium channel block to beta blockade and carries a torsades risk; the short-acting intravenous agent is esmolol.
Correct. Esmolol is the intravenous, short-acting beta blocker.

set1.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of antiarrhythmic drugs
set1.q: A 66-year-old woman takes quinidine to maintain rhythm after atrial flutter. She now reports ringing in her ears, dizziness and blurred vision. Which listed toxicity explains her symptoms?
opts: A lupus-like syndrome belongs to procainamide, more often in slow acetylators, and does not cause tinnitus; this triad is cinchonism.
Hypersensitivity is listed for lidocaine and does not produce ringing ears with dizziness; quinidine's triad is cinchonism.
Thyroid abnormalities belong to amiodarone, a thyroid hormone analog; tinnitus, dizziness and blurred vision are quinidine's cinchonism.
Correct. Cinchonism (tinnitus, dizziness and blurred vision) is on quinidine's toxicity list; quinidine is an isomer of quinine.

set1.q: A 70-year-old man with glaucoma needs a class IA drug for ventricular tachycardia. Which class IA drug is contraindicated for him?
opts: Procainamide has less anticholinergic activity than quinidine and no glaucoma contraindication listed; disopyramide is the one to avoid.
ruled out by a stated finding
Quinidine's anticholinergic action is weaker than disopyramide's, and glaucoma is not on its list; disopyramide is contraindicated.
ruled out by a stated finding
Correct. Disopyramide has more anticholinergic action than quinidine, and glaucoma is on its contraindication list with heart block and hypersensitivity.
Lidocaine is class IB, not IA, and its listed contraindications are seizures and age; disopyramide is contraindicated in glaucoma.

set1.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of antiarrhythmic drugs
set1.q: A 66-year-old man has taken amiodarone for two years. He now has a dry cough, worsening breathlessness and fine crackles at both lung bases. Which listed toxicity is most likely?
opts: Bronchospasm is listed for propranolol and sotalol and causes wheeze rather than crackles; amiodarone causes pulmonary fibrosis.
Respiratory paralysis is listed for magnesium sulfate and does not cause cough and crackles; amiodarone causes pulmonary fibrosis.
Correct. Pneumonitis and pulmonary fibrosis are amiodarone's potentially fatal toxicity, building up on long-term use.
Heart failure is listed for beta blockers, disopyramide and propafenone; on long-term amiodarone, cough with crackles points to fibrosis.

set2.q: A 45-year-old woman with a seizure disorder develops ventricular tachycardia. Which drug's listed contraindications include her seizure disorder?
opts: Correct. Lidocaine's listed contraindications are seizures and age, and its toxicity runs from drowsiness to seizures.
Amiodarone's toxicities are lung, thyroid, skin, eye, nerve and liver effects; seizures are a listed contraindication for lidocaine.
Procainamide's concerns are lupus, marrow suppression and torsades; seizures are a listed contraindication for lidocaine.
Sotalol's toxicities are torsades de pointes and bronchospasm; seizures are a listed contraindication for lidocaine.

set2.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
set2.q: A 61-year-old woman with a structurally normal heart starts flecainide. Her next electrocardiogram shows longer PR, QRS and QT intervals. Which action explains these changes?
opts: Correct. Flecainide blocks sodium and potassium channels in the ventricles and slows sodium channel recovery, prolonging the PR, QRS and QT intervals.
Beta-1 receptor block is the class II mechanism of metoprolol, acting on the nodes; flecainide blocks sodium and potassium channels.
Activating atrial potassium channels is adenosine's action, which hyperpolarizes cells; flecainide blocks sodium and potassium channels.
Sodium-potassium ATPase inhibition is digoxin's mechanism; flecainide blocks sodium and potassium channels.

set2.io: Describe adverse effects of antiarrhythmic drugs
set2.q: A 63-year-old man is receiving intravenous magnesium sulfate for torsades de pointes. Which listed toxicity is the most serious to watch for?
opts: Pulmonary fibrosis is amiodarone's long-term lung toxicity; with magnesium sulfate the serious risk is respiratory paralysis.
Agranulocytosis is listed for propafenone; with magnesium sulfate the serious risk is respiratory paralysis.
Correct. Magnesium sulfate's listed toxicities are bradycardia, flushing, headache and respiratory paralysis, the most serious of these.
Flushing is on magnesium sulfate's list but is the milder effect; respiratory paralysis is the most serious listed toxicity.

set2.io: Outline appropriate patient education for antiarrhythmic drugs
set2.q: A 58-year-old woman is starting long-term amiodarone. Which counseling point addresses a listed skin toxicity?
opts: Flushing after each dose belongs to adenosine (and magnesium sulfate); amiodarone's skin problem is photosensitivity.
A lupus-like syndrome belongs to procainamide, more often in slow acetylators; amiodarone's skin problem is photosensitivity.
Correct. Amiodarone causes photosensitivity and a blue-gray skin color, so sun protection is the counseling point.
Ringing in the ears is part of quinidine's cinchonism, not a skin effect; amiodarone causes photosensitivity.

set2.q: A 71-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation also has heart failure with severely depressed pump function. Which drug is listed to be avoided in her?
opts: Correct. Diltiazem and verapamil are negative inotropes, to be avoided in depressed cardiac function.
Digoxin is listed to slow the ventricular rate in atrial fibrillation; depressed cardiac function is on the avoid list for diltiazem.
Amiodarone's listed dangers are lung, thyroid, eye, skin and liver toxicity; depressed cardiac function is on diltiazem's avoid list.
Dofetilide is listed for normal rhythm in atrial fibrillation, with torsades as its danger; depressed function is on diltiazem's avoid list.

set2.io: Identify indications for commonly used antiarrhythmic drugs
set2.q: A 61-year-old woman taking sotalol faints. The monitor shows a long QT interval and a polymorphic ventricular tachycardia twisting around the baseline. Which intravenous agent is listed for this rhythm?
opts: Adenosine is listed for paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia; torsades de pointes is treated with magnesium sulfate.
Dofetilide causes torsades de pointes with marked QT prolongation, so it would worsen this; magnesium sulfate treats it.
Verapamil is to be avoided in ventricular arrhythmias; torsades de pointes is treated with magnesium sulfate.
Correct. Torsades de pointes, which sotalol can cause, is treated with intravenous magnesium sulfate.

set2.io: Discuss potential drug-drug, drug-food, and drug-herb interactions with antiarrhythmic drugs
set2.q: A 70-year-old man takes digoxin and warfarin. He is started on amiodarone for recurrent ventricular tachycardia. What happens to his digoxin and warfarin levels?
opts: Amiodarone raises these drugs rather than lowering them; digoxin and warfarin are both on its list of increases.
Warfarin rises as well; amiodarone increases both digoxin and warfarin.
Digoxin rises as well; amiodarone increases both digoxin and warfarin.
Correct. Amiodarone increases digoxin and warfarin, as well as flecainide, phenytoin and procainamide.

set2.io: Identify indications for commonly used antiarrhythmic drugs
set2.q: A 60-year-old man has recurrent ventricular tachycardia that has not responded to other antiarrhythmic drugs. Which drug is listed for this situation?
opts: Propranolol is listed for supraventricular arrhythmias, ventricular ectopic beats and myocardial infarction, not resistant ventricular tachycardia.
Correct. Amiodarone is listed for recurrent ventricular tachycardia or fibrillation resistant to other drugs.
Verapamil is to be avoided in ventricular arrhythmias; resistant ventricular tachycardia is an amiodarone indication.
Adenosine is listed for paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia; resistant ventricular tachycardia is an amiodarone indication.

set2.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of antiarrhythmic drugs
set2.q: A 68-year-old man with atrial flutter takes quinidine, metoprolol, warfarin and digoxin. He faints, and the monitor shows a long QT interval followed by a polymorphic ventricular rhythm twisting around the baseline. Which drug most likely caused this rhythm?
opts: Correct. Torsades de pointes (2 to 8%) and quinidine sudden death are on quinidine's toxicity list.
Metoprolol's listed concerns are heart failure, sedation and fatigue; the twisting rhythm with a long QT is quinidine's torsades.
ruled out by a stated finding
Warfarin is an anticoagulant, not an antiarrhythmic, and torsades de pointes is not on its list; torsades is listed for quinidine.
ruled out by a stated finding
Digoxin slows atrioventricular conduction and can induce heart block; torsades with a long QT is listed for quinidine.
ruled out by a stated finding

set2.io: Describe adverse effects of antiarrhythmic drugs
set2.q: A 52-year-old woman known to be a slow acetylator has taken oral procainamide for several months. She now has joint pains, a rash and fever. Which adverse effect is most likely?
opts: Cinchonism (tinnitus, dizziness, blurred vision) is quinidine's; joint pain, rash and fever in a slow acetylator point to procainamide lupus.
Correct. A lupus-like syndrome affects 25 to 50% of patients on procainamide, more often slow acetylators.
Agranulocytosis is listed for propafenone; in a slow acetylator on procainamide, joint pain, rash and fever point to a lupus-like syndrome.
Hypothyroidism is an amiodarone effect; joint pain, rash and fever in a slow acetylator point to procainamide lupus.

set2.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for antiarrhythmic drugs
set2.q: A 64-year-old man is receiving intravenous lidocaine for ventricular premature beats after an acute myocardial infarction. Which finding is the early sign of lidocaine toxicity?
opts: Tinnitus with dizziness and blurred vision is quinidine's cinchonism; the early sign of lidocaine toxicity is nystagmus.
Corneal deposits are an amiodarone toxicity of long-term use; the early sign of lidocaine toxicity is nystagmus.
Flushing is listed for adenosine and magnesium sulfate; the early sign of lidocaine toxicity is nystagmus.
Correct. Nystagmus is the early sign of lidocaine toxicity; drowsiness, confusion, restlessness, twitching and seizures follow.

set2.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
set2.q: A 74-year-old man takes digoxin, and his ventricular rate in atrial fibrillation has slowed. Which action contributes to this effect?
opts: Digoxin indirectly decreases sympathetic tone; raising it would speed the heart. Its slowing comes partly from more parasympathetic tone.
Correct. Digoxin inhibits the sodium-potassium ATPase, slows atrioventricular conduction and indirectly increases parasympathetic tone while decreasing sympathetic tone.
Beta-1 receptor block is the class II action of metoprolol; digoxin slows the rate partly by raising parasympathetic tone.
Potassium channel block is the class III mechanism that prolongs repolarization; digoxin raises parasympathetic tone.

set2.q: A 59-year-old man has sustained ventricular tachycardia after a myocardial infarction. Which drug is listed to be avoided in his arrhythmia?
opts: Amiodarone is listed for recurrent ventricular tachycardia or fibrillation resistant to other drugs; verapamil is to be avoided.
Lidocaine is listed for ventricular tachycardia and acute myocardial infarction; verapamil is to be avoided in ventricular arrhythmias.
Correct. Verapamil and diltiazem are to be avoided in ventricular arrhythmias, sick sinus syndrome and depressed cardiac function.
Procainamide is a class IA drug, and class IA covers ventricular tachycardia; verapamil is to be avoided in ventricular arrhythmias.

set2.io: Identify indications for commonly used antiarrhythmic drugs
set2.q: A 58-year-old man with asthma has atrial fibrillation with a fast ventricular rate. A beta blocker is planned. Which beta blocker is preferred for him?
opts: Propranolol is a nonselective beta blocker with bronchospasm on its toxicity list, so it is the one to avoid in asthma.
ruled out by a stated finding
Sotalol has beta-blocking activity with bronchospasm on its toxicity list and adds potassium channel block; metoprolol is preferred.
ruled out by a stated finding
Propafenone is a class IC drug whose beta-blocking activity brings bronchospasm; metoprolol is the preferred beta-1 selective blocker.
ruled out by a stated finding
Correct. Metoprolol is beta-1 selective and causes less bronchospasm than propranolol, which matters in asthma.
